model_answer:
**Amazon (AMZN)** planned the most capex for 2025 of the three.

Amazon's 2025 capex guidance rose over the year:
- **February 2025:** Amazon said it planned to boost capital expenditures to $100 billion in 2025.
- **October 2025:** It raised its 2025 capex forecast to $125 billion.
- **Actual spend:** Amazon deployed $131.8 billion in capex in 2025. Another source puts the figure at $128.3B, so reported totals differ slightly.

Alphabet (GOOG) and Meta were lower at every point:
- **Alphabet:** In October 2025 it said it expected 2025 capital expenditures of $91 billion to $93 billion. That was up from $85 billion in July and $75 billion in February.
- **Meta:** It started the year with a range of $60-65 billion, then raised it to $64-72 billion in April 2025. One source puts its 2025 actual at roughly $72B.

| Company | 2025 capex plan (latest guidance) |
|---|---|
| Amazon | ~$125B (actual ~$128–132B) |
| Alphabet | $91–93B |
| Meta | $64–72B |

Amazon's lead is expected to continue in 2026, when Amazon is projecting $200 billion in capital expenditures.
judge_reason: Correctly picks AMZN and gives the initial GOOG and META figures, but commits to later-revised AMZN capex (~$125B) instead of $105.2B and presents revised guidance that conflicts with the official figures.
